newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA M2 UP 18.1 PCT END-JULY YR/YR-CENTRAL BANK.
newsitem.headline: CHINA M2 UP 18.1 PCT END-JULY YR/YR-CENTRAL BANK.

text.p: China's broad M2 money supply rose by 18.1 percent year-on-year at the end of July, to 8,350 bilion yuan, the central bank, the People's Bank of China, said in a statement on Thursday.
That marked a decline of 7.2 percentage points compared with the end of last year, it said.
China's M1, or cash in circulation plus current business deposits, was up 18.4 percent at the end of July year-on-year, to 3,110 billion yuan, the central bank said.
That level was unchanged from the end of 1996, it said, but gave no further details.
M0, or cash in circulation, was put at 10.9 percent of M2 at the end of June this year, it said, but did not elaborate. At end June, M2 was up 19.1 percent.
China's M1 was up a year-on-year 20.6 percent at the end of June, while M0 was up 19 percent, bank figures showed earlier.
At the end of the first quarter, M2 was up 21.1 percent, while M1 was up 18.4 percent and M0 rose 13.6 percent.
The government has said it expects M2 to grow by 24.5 percent in 1997 and M1 by about 18 percent.
China's M2 grew by 25.3 percent last year, while M1 was up 18.9 percent and M0 rose 11.6 percent.
